chapter: The Savoy band and the Swing era
title: The Savoy Ballroom and its dances
summary: He recalls the Savoy's bands and the Lindy Hop and Big Apple; they called the music swing but had no idea it would spread.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Uh huh. Did that band have any broadcasts?
Yes.
No. Not that I remember.
Broadcasts from the Savoy Ballroom came later.
In 1939 ... 1938 maybe, I don't know.
Uh huh. When did the Savoy open? Do you remember off hand?
I believe it was 1927.
Yes. And what kind of bands had they had there before? Had Chick Webb already played the Savoy by 1933, do you remember?
Well, Chick played there I think in 1931.
Earlier, I think so, yes.
You played with him then.
Yeah.
Uh huh.
But they had had, oh, they had Fess Williams.
Right.

And they had Leon Abbey. They had someone else whose name I can't remember at the moment. I can see his face before me, but I can't remember the name. MR. BERGER: Was the music you played there in this early time, early in the sense that it was in the early thirties, was that the kind of music that would be called Swing?
I suppose so, yes.
This was when the dancers were doing, what? What kind of dances were they doing?
Oh, they called it the Lindy Hop.
The Lindy Hop ... and the Big Apple? That was something else that was hot then.
Yes, The Big Apple, too. Yes.
That was not a dance between two people, that was a group, I think, dance, or something, wasn't it?
The Big Apple? No, that was a dance between 2 people. Yes.
And so at that time there were a lot of these jump junk tunes, you might call them, you know -- that people danced to.
Uh huh.
But, again, you didn't think of this
as Swing music or this kind of music or that kind of music -- you didn't think that you were now introducing something which would become known and spread all over the world as Swing music?
No. I had no idea. But we did call it Swing, you know.

Yeah. You did what you wanted. You were playing the kind of music that you wanted -- not consciously doing something that you thought that audience wanted. You were consciously trying to please an audience, dancers -- but it was in a way, in the same general direction that you yourself wanted to go and play.
Yes.
And your musicians.
Surely.
Right.
Yes.
